What SteinJobs does

About this demo

SteinJobs is the outbound engine Eric Steinberg built to run his own early-stage job search like signal-based prospecting: find the right startups, catch them at the right moment, and reach the founder instead of applying cold. This page is a public snapshot of the real app.

  • Real: the code, and every posting: public listings from startup job boards, VC portfolio boards, company ATS pages and SEC filings, scored by the real scorer.
  • Fictional: every person (founders, contacts, connections), every pipeline stage, note and streak. A blank-beats-a-guess rule governs the real app; here the people are invented on purpose so no real inbox is ever implied.
  • Stack: Python stdlib server with zero dependencies, a single-file UI, Claude Haiku scoring through the Batch API (about $0.56 per 500 postings), SEC EDGAR Form D for funding signals.
  • Measured: founder lookup by source: SEC Form D found 1 of 12, scraping company sites found 0 of 67, LLM web search found 16 of 17.
  • Code: github.com/rojomuchachos/steinjobs-demo

The job: find early-stage startup roles, the companies behind them, and the people to write to — then track every thread until it closes. It scores each posting 0–100 against Eric's rubric (role shape 35% · stage 25% · industry 20% · location 10% · comp 10%), and it never writes resumes or emails: it puts the right person, the right timing, and the right proof point in front of you, and stops.

What gets found

  • Pre-seed → Series A (B only for explicit 0→1 builds); high-agency generalist shapes — founding/early, growth, BD, chief of staff who builds, PM, technical-GTM.
  • Sweet spot: health & human performance. Interest exceptions with real history: music, psychedelics/mental health, neuro tools, food systems tech, ed-tech, civic tech, fitness, outdoors.
  • Hard-excluded at import: pure IC data science, big-company seats (and mega-corp careers hosts), consulting, senior titles, AE/AM/CS/designer execution seats, internships, postings asking for graduate degrees.
  • NYC first, SF fine, remote for the right company; Europe only with sponsorship (Eric is a US citizen), judged against local comp.

How a posting flows

Scout (daily) → prefilter → score → Review pile → triage ✓/✕ → Saved → tracker board (applied → interviewing → offer) → sends & follow-ups (nudges at day 4 and 11 — two is the whole budget). Postings scoring ≤50 auto-pass; stale review ages out (Auto-Swept); pages that 404 become expired — both hide behind the Auto-Swept lens. Postings arriving without a description wait as incomplete, invisible until text and a score promote them.

The rules the data lives by

  • No blind scoring — no description, no score, ever.
  • Never invent founders, emails, stages, descriptions. A blank beats a guess.
  • Duplicates backfill blanks only; they never overwrite a recorded value.
  • Acquired brands resolve to their acquirer.
  • A person's warm signals come only from their own verified text — never from Eric-side context.
  • LinkedIn and Wellfound are reached only through Eric's real Chrome, on request.

Reading the cards

  • Glyphs: 🔥 warm · 🎓 multi-school alum · 🦅 Emory · 🐗 NMH · 🌱 pre-seed · 🌳 seed · $A/$B+ later rounds · 💰 raised (fresh <30d goes green) · 🗽 🌉 🍀 🌐 cities, country flags abroad. Open any card and glyphs speak in words.
  • Gray company card = no description or industry yet; dashed +N = fields missing; muted card = you already opened it; loud green posting = offer. The muted intel line on a posting ("raised 2mo ago · ~12 ppl · 3 roles in the feed") is the why-now at a glance; slow apply flags long-form ATS hosts.

It learns from you

Every pass-with-a-reason becomes a worked example the scorer reads next time. Insights reports where the scorer disagrees with your actual verdicts, which sources earn their keep, and which proof points open doors.
